subject: Post-demo triage: truncation scenarios and model fit recommendations
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Beth Carter <beth@hightidehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo triage: truncation scenarios and model fit recommendations

Hi Beth — great to meet today, thanks for walking us through the Hightide care workflow and the sample visit bundles. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of call notes
- Primary goal: automated visit-summary + problem list extraction across 10–30 pages of notes per patient.
- Key constraints: (1) high summarization fidelity for medication changes, (2) minimal hallucinations on diagnosis history, (3) 99.9% PII retention policy means we must avoid sending raw PHI to third parties in some flows.
- Current throughput target: 50 summaries/minute for peak-hour processing.

Initial fit observations (from our demo session)
- Short-run QA: model variants with 32k+ context are useful but we observed truncation at synthetic 40k inputs when using standard chunking.
- Summarization fidelity: longer-context models keep more history but occasionally conflate temporally-separated events when prompts are not anchored.

Recommended models & configs to evaluate (first pass)
- Redwood-Chat-13B-extended (q4o): baseline for cost-sensitive runs (good at structured extraction with prompt templates).
- Redwood-Llama-70B-4k & 32k variants (baseline + long-context): use 32k for end-to-end summary trials; keep 4k as a fallback for fast, cheap micro-batches.
- rwkv-14B-long (experimental): promising for sustained long attention on concatenated notes; try with KV-cache-friendly runtime.

Planned benchmark items (what we'll run next)
1) Truncation matrix: feed synthetic concatenations of visit notes (5k, 15k, 30k, 45k, 60k) and record where critical fields (med changes, diagnoses) are lost.
2) Prompt anchoring test: measure fidelity with and without anchored date/patient-context tokens in the prompt.
3) Regression smoke tests: use your flagged prompt set plus 150 historical visits to check hallucination rates and factual drop-off.

Attachments I’m sending: hightide_prompt_suite_v1.jsonl (seed prompts + expected answer keys), benchmark_results_truncation_cases.csv (initial synthetic matrix from demo).

Concrete next steps
- We’ll run the truncation matrix across the three variants above and share a short results spreadsheet by EOD Tuesday.
- Karthik will propose a specific pilot configuration (instances, batching, KV cache settings) after we see the initial numbers.
- Would you be able to share one de-identified bundle (S3 link or Drive) that represents a 30–60 page visit record? That will let us reproduce the truncation behavior end-to-end.

If that all sounds right I’ll schedule a 30-minute follow-up for Tuesday (10/6) to run through the results.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs:
- hightide_prompt_suite_v1.jsonl (application/jsonl)
- benchmark_results_truncation_cases.csv (text/csv)

Lauren — thanks for the clear recap and action plan. A few clarifications from our side before you run the matrix: 

1) De-identified bundle: we can provide a sample but it will still include some structured PHI placeholders. Would you prefer an S3 pre-signed link or a Drive folder?
2) Hallucination tolerances: our clinical ops team requires <1% false-positive critical diagnosis in the summary. How do you suggest we measure that in the regression smoke tests?
3) Throughput: 50 summaries/minute — what's your expectation for instance sizing with the 32k Redwood-Llama variant?

Also looping in procurement (procure@hightidehealth.com) to flag enterprise security and SLA questions early.

Thanks,
Beth

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

On Mon, Oct 5, 2026 at 9:04 AM Beth Carter <beth@hightidehealth.com> wrote:
> 1) De-identified bundle: we can provide a sample but it will still include some structured PHI placeholders. Would you prefer an S3 pre-signed link or a Drive folder?
> 2) Hallucination tolerances: our clinical ops team requires <1% false-positive critical diagnosis in the summary. How do you suggest we measure that in the regression smoke tests?
> 3) Throughput: 50 summaries/minute — what's your expectation for instance sizing with the 32k Redwood-Llama variant?

Thanks for the questions — quick answers: 
- Share via S3 pre-signed link; we'll pull into a sandbox VPC space and run the pipeline without external model-hosted PHI leaving Hightide's control. If Drive is easier for you we can accept that but prefer S3 for production parity.
- Measurement approach for hallucinations: we will run the 150-case regression set and compute two metrics: (a) false-positive critical diagnosis rate (exact string match against expected keys, normalized per-case), and (b) information loss rate for medication changes (percentage of expected med-change events missing). We’ll flag any case where either metric exceeds thresholds and include example failure traces.
- Instance sizing estimate (very rough initial projection): for Redwood-Llama-32k around 70–90 summaries/minute per four-GPU (A100) pool when using batch size 8 + KV cache pinned per session. We will instrument and refine. For the 70B single-node setups throughput drops but per-summary latency improves for single-request workflows.

Planned immediate runs (this week): 
1) Truncation matrix: run on 5k/15k/30k/45k sequences across Redwood-Chat-13B-extended (q4o), Redwood-Llama-32k, and rwkv-14B-long. Expect results file by Tue EOD (10/6).
2) Regression smoke: run your 150-case set (if you can share) against the same variants — deliver a short report with metrics and 10 example failures.

We’ll also include a short prompt-anchoring experiment (with anchored date + section headers) to see fidelity gains.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Beth Carter <beth@hightidehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo triage: truncation scenarios and model fit recommendations

Thanks Karthik — S3 presigned link is best. I just asked our security team for a single de-identified bundle (30 pages, contains placeholders for PHI). They said they can deliver by COB today. Two quick asks before we proceed: 

- Can you include a short runbook for how you perform the de-identification checks? Our security lead wants to know whether Redwood runs any entity-recognition pass or relies on our de-id process.
- In the regression report, please surface any cases where the model produced a confident but incorrect diagnosis (not partials) as a separate list — we need those to assess clinical risk.

If you can confirm those points I’ll send the S3 link once the bundle is ready.

Best,
Beth
Beth Carter
Head of Clinical Product, Hightide Health
